variety: Cabécar, primarily the northern (Chirripó) dialect as used in the Bible.is New Testament (CJPTJV, the MMS-TTS training text) and Margery's d.n. forms; general (unmarked) dictionary forms preferred; southern (d.s./Ujarrás/SJC) forms used only where no northern/general form was found and flagged in note.
orthography: MMS-TTS cjp (Bible.is CJPTJV) orthography: nasal vowels with combining macron below U+0331 (a̱ e̱ i̱ o̱ u̱ ä̱ ë̱ ö̱), ä ë ö for the extra vowels, ñ, j=/h/, sh, ch, tk, ts, k'. Model vocab (vocab.json) has a à á ä è é ë í ó ö ú ñ, U+0331 and apostrophe; no ì/ò/ù/ü or combining acute, so tone accents on ë/ö are dropped in synthesis. Words attested in the Bible are given in Bible spelling; dictionary-only words keep Margery 1989 spelling (his underline for nasality rendered as U+0331; his acute tone marks kept). Margery writes some vowels differently from the Bible (e.g. dayë vs däyë, tkabë vs tkäbe, ká̱ wö́ vs ka̱wä) — a reviewer should normalise to one standard (MEP/UCR alphabet, González Campos & Obando 2017) before recording.

sources.title: Diccionario cabécar-español, español-cabécar
sources.author: Enrique Margery Peña
sources.note: Editorial de la Universidad de Costa Rica; scan formerly hosted by UCR INIL (now 404, archived). Cited by entry number; dialect labels d.n. (northern/Chirripó), d.s. (southern), Uj. (Ujarrás), Ch. (Chirripó), SJC (San José Cabécar), LE (La Estrella).

sources.title: facebook/mms-tts-cjp model card, vocab.json and tokenizer_config.json (is_uroman=false)
sources.author: Meta AI (Pratap et al., Scaling Speech Technology to 1,000+ Languages)

jaguar.note: General (unmarked) form. d.n. synonym satálá (entry 5405). SENSITIVE: the jaguar has ritual weight in Cabécar practice; the dictionary lists na_má_ bata (ceremonial helper, 4517) and na_má_ dalí 'enfermedad del tigre', a taboo-linked illness (4518). Plain noun is everyday vocabulary.
jaguar.reviewQuestion: ¿Se usa 'na̱má̱' para el jaguar con niños sin problema, o prefieren 'satálá' (Chirripó)?

colibri.note: Southern-dialect form. The northern (d.n.) generic is ma_tsu_ (entry ~4295), but the dictionary also gives ma_tsu_ (d.n., vulg.) 'pene' — avoided for a children's game. batsu_ is also a dog's name in San José Cabécar (SJC). Chirripó speakers may expect ma_tsu_.
colibri.reviewQuestion: ¿Cómo dicen 'colibrí' en su comunidad: 'batsu̱' o 'ma̱tsu̱'? ¿'ma̱tsu̱' tiene un doble sentido que no conviene para niños?

llama.source: none found in margery1989 or Bible.is CJPTJV
llama.note: Andean animal with no Cabécar term in the dictionary. The Bible translation borrows Spanish names for foreign animals ('camello', 'oveja', 'cabra'), so a Spanish loan 'llama' is plausible, but it is unattested here; left null rather than guessed.
llama.reviewQuestion: ¿Dirían simplemente 'llama' (en español) o hay otra forma?

condor.note: Not a Costa Rican bird; no entry. The closest native concept is olo 'zopilote' (vulture, Bible.is Mt 24:28) and an entry for 'zopilote rey' (king vulture), but neither is a condor. Left null.
condor.reviewQuestion: ¿Usarían 'cóndor' prestado del español, o el nombre del zopilote rey?

mariposa.note: General form. d.n. variant kuák'a (3950, marked p.u. 'poco usado'). Night moths: kuákua yee (d.n.) 'mariposa nocturna'.

guajolote.note: General form. Short one-syllable word: check it is distinct enough in audio from other cho-/chö- words.

tortuga.note: General form kuë; Chirripó (d.n.) k'uë́ with glottalized k'. Tone mark on the general form not verified on the scan. Note: in the southern dialect kuë also means 'maíz' (entry ~4044) — homonym risk in a game that also has a maize card.
tortuga.reviewQuestion: ¿Dicen 'kuë' o 'k'uë' para tortuga? ¿En su zona 'kuë' también es maíz?

rana.note: General form. Ch. variant yökok (p.u.). Do not confuse with buki/buke 'sapo' (toad, 647; Bible.is Rev 16:13 'buke'); buki also has a vulgar sense ('vulva', 647) — another reason to prefer bulbí.

serpiente.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 10:16, Lk 10:19 'tkäbe'; margery1989 entry 6784 tkabë (generic)
serpiente.note: Bible spelling (matches MMS-TTS training text); dictionary writes tkabë, d.s. tkebë (6811), SJC chabe (734). Snakes are associated with healers/taboos in Cabécar tradition; neutral as a noun.

maiz.note: Northern (Chirripó) form. Southern form kuë (d.s., ~4044) is homonymous with 'turtle'. Maize has ceremonial uses (chicha), but the word is everyday.
maiz.reviewQuestion: ¿'Ik'uö' es la forma usada en su comunidad para maíz?

nopal.note: Opuntia is not part of the Talamanca/Chirripó environment; no entry. Left null.
nopal.reviewQuestion: ¿Existe un nombre cabécar para este cactus, o se usaría 'nopal'?

frijol.note: General form; d.n./Uj. k'a_ní_ (3330) with glottalized k'. ka_ní_ kicharaga 'vainica' (green bean pod).

pina.note: General form, two words as printed. Tone accents (í, ö́) as in the dictionary; MMS vocab has no combining acute so the accent on ö is dropped in synthesis.

chile.note: General form. SJC dapa/dapo/dipa; Uj. baka shi 'chile de ganado'. One-syllable word.

papa.source: no Cabécar term in margery1989 (only baga kiwö 'papa chiricana', a different tuber, entry 141)
papa.note: Potato is not a traditional Cabécar crop. Spanish loan offered on the Bible.is precedent of keeping Spanish nouns for introduced items; not attested in Cabécar sources. Homophone risk: Spanish 'papá'.
papa.reviewQuestion: ¿Dicen 'papa' en español para la papa, o hay otra palabra?

aguacate.note: General form; also jo_mó_ (2356) and d.n. a_mó_ (98). ja_mó_ klö́ = avocado tree.

tomate.source: no Cabécar term for cultivated tomato in margery1989; wild relative shalbo (d.n., 5985) 'tomate de montaña' (Cyphomandra)
tomate.note: Cultivated tomato has no entry. shalbo names a different wild plant, so it is not offered as the card word. Spanish loan, unattested in Cabécar sources.

girasol.note: Southern-dialect only; no northern form found. Nasal underlines read from the scan (u, í) — verify.

sol.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 24:29, Rev 10:1, Rev 12:1 'ka̱wä'; margery1989 entry 3085 ká_ wö́ 'sol'
sol.note: Bible spelling (MMS training text). Dictionary: ká_ wö́ (general), kö́wö́ and k'á_ wö (d.n.). The sun figures in Cabécar cosmology (Sibö's creation narratives) — neutral as a noun but note for reviewers.

luna.note: Same in dictionary and Bible. tulu balá = full moon (6730).

estrella.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 2:2, Mt 24:29, Rev 12:1 'bekwä'; margery1989 entry 312 béi wö́ (d.n.), margery1989 entry 316 bék wö́ (d.s.)
estrella.note: Bible spelling chosen for MMS. Dictionary forms are written as two words (béi wö́ / bék wö́); bekwä appears to be the same word written together.

lluvia.note: Bible spelling; dictionary accents the second syllable. ka_lí_ bulána 'llover'.

rayo.note: Northern form. d.s. tala wö́rkua (6435). The Bible renders lightning as 'ka̱ wäju̱r' (Mt 28:3, Lk 10:18), which may be a verb phrase ('it flashes'). Thunder is tala bula (Rev 4:5). Storms/thunder have spiritual associations; neutral as noun.
rayo.reviewQuestion: ¿Para el rayo dicen 'kuálklö', 'tala wörkua' o 'ka̱ wäju̱r'?

arcoiris.note: Bible spelling; d.s. shkabä (also 'halo of sun/moon'). In many Chibchan traditions the rainbow is an omen; check whether it carries a taboo for children.
arcoiris.reviewQuestion: ¿'Shikaba' es el arcoíris? ¿Tiene algún significado delicado?

nube.source: margery1989 entry 4369 (s. cl. pl.) 'nube'; bibleis-cjptjv Mt 24:30, Rev 10:1 'mo̱'
nube.note: Same in dictionary and Bible. One-syllable word.

viento.source: margery1989 entry 5682 si_wá_ 'viento', 'aire', 'historia, leyenda'; bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:25 'si̱wa̱'
viento.note: SENSITIVE: si_wá_ also means traditional/sacred knowledge and narratives ('historia', 'leyenda'); using it for wind is normal everyday speech, but reviewers should confirm it is fine on a game card.
viento.reviewQuestion: ¿'Si̱wa̱' para el viento en un juego infantil está bien, dado que también significa la historia/sabiduría tradicional?

cometa.note: No word for 'comet' found; this is the southern term for a meteor/shooting star (d.n. equivalent at entry 370, not verified on scan). Bible Mt 24:29 'bekwä jolortémi' = 'stars will fall'. SENSITIVE: the dictionary records fiery streaks in the sky (ja_má_ júr, mit., 1908) as omens of calamity — confirm the shooting-star word is not ominous for children.
cometa.reviewQuestion: ¿Hay palabra para 'cometa'? ¿La estrella fugaz se considera mal presagio?

montana.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 5:14, Mt 17:1 'ka̱tsä (bata)'; margery1989 entry 2928 ká_ bata 'cerro, montaña'
montana.note: Bible spelling. Dictionary: ká_ tsö (s. cl. red.) and ká_ bata (generic). Some mountains (e.g. Chirripó peaks) are sacred places; the generic noun is neutral.

volcan.note: No native term found. Bible Rev 8:8 describes 'something like a great mountain burning' descriptively. Spanish loan, unattested.
volcan.reviewQuestion: ¿Cómo llaman a un volcán (p. ej. el Turrialba)?

manantial.note: Northern form (díglö 'water'; Bible writes diklä). d.s. díglö yölí (1142); Ch. bölë. Bible Jas 3:11 uses a verb phrase 'diklä tsikirke̱ ska'. Springs can be spiritually significant places.
manantial.reviewQuestion: ¿'Díglö tsi̱ní̱' es el ojo de agua/naciente?

mar.source: bibleis-cjptjv Acts 27:41, Rev 4:6 'däyë'; margery1989 entry 1040 dayë 'mar', 'sal'
mar.note: Bible spelling (dictionary dayë). Same word means 'salt'.

desierto.note: The Bible's rendering of Spanish 'desierto' (wilderness). Lit. roughly 'empty/abandoned place'; it does not evoke sand dunes. Long phrase for a card.
desierto.reviewQuestion: ¿Hay una palabra más corta para desierto, o se usaría 'desierto' en español?

selva.note: Northern form; d.s. kal gi_ (2721). ká_ bata 'cerro' also extends to 'monte'.

cristal.note: No native word for crystal/gem found. The Bible uses the Spanish loan 'vidrio' where Spanish has 'cristal'. 'jak' = stone.
cristal.reviewQuestion: ¿Para un cristal de roca usarían 'vidrio', 'jak' u otra palabra?

isla.note: Bible term; däyë 'sea'. Dictionary only has díglö wöbla (d.s., 1196) 'small river island'.

cueva.source: not found in margery1989 (closest: k'olöi d.n. 'hueco de cierta extensión y profundidad', 3393 area)
cueva.note: No clear noun for 'cave' found. Bible Heb 11:38 'ka̱ wäja̱r' / 'ishäkä wäja̱r' may mean 'holes/caves of the earth' but the gloss is uncertain. Caves can be sacred/burial places in Talamanca tradition. Left null.

olla.source: margery1989 entry 3084 (s. cl. red.) 'olla de barro'
olla.note: Matches the art (clay pot). Generic 'olla' is u_ (7374), a single nasal vowel — too short for a card.
olla.reviewQuestion: ¿'Ká̱ wí̱' es la olla de barro?

cesto.source: margery1989 entry 523 (s. cl. red.) 'canasto'; (s. cl. pl.) 'bolso pequeño'
cesto.note: General form. Other baskets: jokóbölo (d.s.), kok'óbölo (d.n.). Bible uses Spanish 'canasta' (Mt 14:20).

tambor.note: General form; SJC bak (154). Drums accompany ceremonies and chichadas; neutral as a noun.

adobe.source: none in margery1989 (dù 'barro, lodo', 1278, is mud, not brick)
adobe.note: Adobe construction is not traditional in the region; no term. Left null.
adobe.reviewQuestion: ¿Hay forma de decir 'adobe' o se usaría el español?

hilo.note: General form (tulúk = needle). Uj. ja_má_ kséi (1910).

canoa.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 13:2, Acts 27:44 'ko̱no'; margery1989 entry 3838 kö_no_ 'bote', 'canoa'

puente.note: Primary meaning is rope/vine; 'bridge' sense marked p.u. (rarely used) — fits a hanging/rope bridge. Nasal/tone marking not verified on the scan; Bible uses ksa̱ for 'sand' (Mt 7:26), so tone/nasality distinguishes homonyms.

vela.source: bibleis-cjptjv Lk 15:8, Rev 4:5 'tsi̱ni'; margery1989 entry 7127 tsini (d.n.) 'candela', 'luz'
vela.note: Bible spelling (lamp). General dictionary form tsa_ni_ (7007) 'hule', 'candela', 'luz' — also means rubber/resin.

martillo.note: No native term found (dictionary 'martilla' is an animal, kinkajou). Spanish loan, unattested.

casa.source: margery1989 entry 2368 (s. cl. pl.) 'casa' (genérico), 'rancho'; bibleis-cjptjv Mt 7:24-27 'ju'
casa.note: Same in dictionary and Bible. Traditional conical house (usulë) is a sacred structure — the generic ju is neutral.

milpa.note: General form; d.n. të́i (6519) and ik'uö́ të́i (1611).

tienda.note: Southern form; no northern form found. Bible uses 'jile watju̱aklä jui' (house of selling, Jn 2:16).

plaza.source: bibleis-cjptjv Mt 11:16, Mt 20:3, Acts 17:17 'sa tapanaklä däli watju̱ak shtä ska'
plaza.note: Shortened from the Bible's phrase for 'marketplace/plaza' ('where we gather, where things are sold'). The shortening is mine — reviewers must confirm it stands alone.
plaza.reviewQuestion: ¿'Sa tapanaklä' se entiende como plaza? ¿O usan 'plaza'?

puerto.note: Bible term ('where boats arrive'), also used in the place name 'Buenos Puertos'.

pueblo.note: Bible term for town/city. Dictionary d.n. ju k'ö́lö́ yökö (2408) 'pueblo, ranchería'.

escuela.source: bibleis-cjptjv Acts 19:9 'Tirano wa̱ sä yuäklä jui' (Spanish 'escuela de Tirano')
escuela.note: Bible descriptive rendering of 'escuela'. Modern Cabécar communities with MEP schools probably use the Spanish loan 'escuela'; unverified.

observatorio.note: No attested term; any phrase would be invented. Left null.

biblioteca.note: No attested term (dictionary has ayë k'uö 'papel, libro' d.n., entry 84, but no 'library'). Left null rather than compose a phrase.
